Registry objectives for topic 4, syllabus-exclusions.json, misconception entries 005/011/014/019. not_checked: Deterministic checks (arithmetic, references, coverage counts, scope scan) were not redone, per the brief. AO/Bloom/command-word/tariff labels were not assessed. Held figure VIS-6116-4.2.2-06 was judged only for wording and the biological answer (item 031: sound). semantic_reviews.reconstruction_test: q6_learner_test: OBJ-6116-4.4.2-07 (ITEM-6116-4-P02, 8 marks): from the notes alone, (a) tt, (b) tall, (c) Tt x Tt, gametes T/t, offspring TT Tt Tt tt, 3 tall : 1 short, (d) 150, (e) chance/ratio is a probability. Full 8/8. OBJ-6116-4.3.5-04/05 (ITEM-6116-4-P03, 10 marks): the notes support (a)-(f) fully (independent variable, 2 mm rule, percentage method, pattern, controlled variables, drying as a second variable). (g) the interval point is not in the notes (4-014), so likely 9/10. Flashcard-type records sampled: 009 meiosis def, 022 sexual reproduction def, 043 progesterone sources, 064 vasectomy/ligation, 098 gene def, 126 ABO blood group. All answerable from the notes alone. 097 diploid is also answerable from the notes, but see 4-004 on its marking. q7_misconceptions: 150 (MISCON-005 mitosis vs meiosis): discriminates. The learner must use the 16 to 8 count to reject mitosis, and the stem does not name meiosis. 151 (MISCON-011 petals vs sepals): discriminates moderately. The learner must name petals and give both functions; the stem says only that the label is wrong. 152 (MISCON-014 genotype vs phenotype): weak, because the stem points to the answer (4-015). 153 (MISCON-019 embryo vs fetus): does not test the entry at all, because it tests egg vs fetus (4-003).

issues.finding: The section first states correctly that maternal and fetal blood are kept separate and do not mix, then says the mother's lungs and kidneys clean 'the blood that she shares with the fetus'. The blood is not shared; only substances are exchanged across the placenta. The same paragraph also says the fetus does not excrete for itself, whereas the fetus does make urea (and urine); it relies on the placenta to pass the urea to the mother.
issues.educational_consequence: A learner may write that maternal and fetal blood mix or are shared, which loses the mark on placental exchange and contradicts the card they learned from.
issues.recommended_repair: Replace 'from the blood that she shares with the fetus through the placenta' with 'after these wastes have diffused from the fetal blood into her blood in the placenta'. Rephrase 'does not breathe or excrete for itself' to 'cannot get rid of its carbon dioxide and urea by its own lungs and kidneys, so they pass to the mother's blood'.
issues.resolution: 4.3.2 placenta notes: fetus makes CO2 and urea but cannot remove them with its own lungs/kidneys; they diffuse into the mother's blood in the placenta and her organs remove them. 'Shared blood' wording removed. Word-neutral (unit stays at 1,240). (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: The statement that a mutation is passed on only if it happens in a cell that makes gametes is true only for sexual reproduction (in animals). In asexual reproduction, which the same notes teach (binary fission, tubers, mitosis copying the parent 'apart from the rare mutation'), a mutation in an ordinary cell is passed to the offspring. The condition has been dropped.
issues.educational_consequence: A learner may deny that a mutation in a bacterium or in a potato tuber can be inherited, which undermines the antibiotic-resistance explanation in 4.4.4 (a chance mutation in a bacterium is passed to all its offspring).
issues.recommended_repair: Add the condition: 'In animals and other organisms that reproduce sexually, a mutation is passed to offspring only if it happens in a cell that makes gametes. In asexual reproduction, such as binary fission, the mutation is copied into the offspring.'
issues.resolution: 4.4.3: rule now limited to animals (gamete-forming cells); added that in asexual reproduction such as binary fission a mutation in the parent cell is copied into the offspring. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: The item is tagged to misconception entry MISCON-6116-019, which is 'embryo vs fetus'. The item tests 'unfertilised egg called a fetus', which is a different confusion (gamete vs developing organism). It never asks the learner to tell an embryo from a fetus, so the entry it claims to address is not tested.
issues.educational_consequence: The embryo/fetus confusion recorded in the curriculum stays untested; the coverage report shows the misconception as handled when it is not.
issues.recommended_repair: Rewrite the stem around the embryo/fetus distinction without a week number (per the entry's authoring constraint), e.g. 'A learner calls a ball of cells that has just implanted a fetus. Explain why embryo is the better term, and when fetus is used.' Answer: early stage, organs forming, is the embryo; later stage, organs present and mainly growing in size, is the fetus. Or re-tag the current item to a different entry.
issues.resolution: ITEM 4.3.2-05 MISCON rewritten around embryo vs fetus with no week number: two learners call a just-implanted ball of cells an embryo or a fetus; learner chooses and says when the other term is used. Answer and 2-mark guidance rewritten; tariff/AO/subtype unchanged. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: The second mark requires 'one set coming from each parent, so the chromosomes form homologous pairs'. The syllabus definition (OBJ-6116-4.4.1-04) is 'a nucleus containing two sets of chromosomes (e.g. in body cells)'. A learner who writes the syllabus definition verbatim, including the example, earns only 1 of 2 marks, while the example 'in body cells' carries no credit.
issues.educational_consequence: Learners are penalised for giving the exact syllabus definition, and are pushed to memorise an addition that the syllabus does not ask for.
issues.recommended_repair: Make the second mark 'e.g. in body cells' (or accept either the example or one set from each parent), or reduce the item to 1 mark.
issues.resolution: ITEM-6116-4-097-DEF second mark now for where the nucleus is found (e.g. body cells), with 'one set from each parent' accepted instead. Syllabus definition now earns 2/2. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: The notes say that, because two gametes fuse in self-pollination, 'the offspring are not identical to the parent'. This is stated unconditionally. A plant that is homozygous at its genes (common in regularly self-pollinating crops such as the beans named in 4.2.2) gives offspring that are genetically the same as the parent. The valid point is that self-pollination is sexual because gametes fuse, not that the offspring must differ.
issues.educational_consequence: A learner may use 'offspring differ from the parent' as the test for sexual reproduction and misclassify cases.
issues.recommended_repair: Change to 'so two gametes fuse and the offspring can differ from the parent. The fusion of gametes, not the result, makes it sexual reproduction.'
issues.resolution: 4.2.1: self-pollination offspring 'can differ'; added that the fusion of gametes, not the result, makes it sexual. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: After saying 'about a quarter should be rr', the notes give 'the expected 1:3'. Everywhere else in 4.4.2 the ratio is written dominant first as 3 : 1. '1:3' is correct only as rr : not-rr and reads as a reversed 3 : 1.
issues.educational_consequence: A learner may write the expected ratio for Rr x Rr as 1 : 3 dominant : recessive.
issues.recommended_repair: Write 'closer to the expected 3 dominant : 1 recessive (one quarter rr)'.
issues.resolution: 4.4.2 simulation: 'expected 3 dominant : 1 recessive (one quarter rr)'. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: The rationale for distractor D is wrong. Option D says 'Reproductive success becomes irrelevant'; the key says D 'removes the mechanism of inheritance'. D removes unequal reproductive success (the selection step), not inheritance.
issues.educational_consequence: A learner reading the key is told the wrong reason the option fails.
issues.recommended_repair: Change to 'D denies the unequal reproductive success that natural selection depends on.'
issues.resolution: P01 Q11 key: D denies the unequal reproductive success that natural selection depends on. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: The canonical answer says the corpus luteum 'does not form normally', while the marking guidance says 'no corpus luteum forms'. The two disagree on the claim credited.
issues.educational_consequence: A marker may withhold or give the mark inconsistently.
issues.recommended_repair: Use one wording in both, e.g. 'the egg is not released and no corpus luteum forms'.
issues.resolution: ITEM 4.3.1 APP (047) answer now 'the egg is not released and no corpus luteum forms', matching guidance. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: Wrong cross-reference: drawing skills are placed in Topic 3, but the registry puts 'make a clear, labelled line drawing' and drawing magnification in Topic 1 (OBJ-6116-1.2.6-12, -13). Microscope use is in Topic 3 (OBJ-6116-3.1-02).
issues.educational_consequence: A learner looking for drawing rules looks in the wrong topic.
issues.recommended_repair: Change to 'Microscope skills are in Topic 3; drawing and measurement skills are in Topic 1.'
issues.resolution: 4.1 cross-reference: microscope skills Topic 3; drawing and measurement skills Topic 1. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: The Namibian dispersal example may name the wrong plant. The plant of the Kalahari sands whose fruit has hooks that catch on animals' feet and fur is devil's claw (Harpagophytum). 'Devil's thorn' usually refers to Tribulus, whose fruit has sharp spines, not hooks. Not certain: local common names vary.
issues.educational_consequence: A learner may give a wrongly matched local example; low impact on marks.
issues.recommended_repair: Check against a Namibian source. Either rename it devil's claw (Harpagophytum procumbens) or describe Tribulus fruit as spiny.
issues.resolution: Renamed to devil's claw (Harpagophytum, hooked 'grapple' fruit). Teacher may confirm local name. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: 'The ovary is not joined directly to the uterus, so there is a short gap that the egg crosses' puts the gap in the wrong place. The gap the egg crosses is between the ovary and the funnel of the oviduct, not between the ovary and the uterus.
issues.educational_consequence: A learner may picture the egg moving directly from the ovary to the uterus across a gap.
issues.recommended_repair: Change to 'The ovary is not joined directly to the oviduct, so the egg crosses a short gap into the oviduct's funnel.'
issues.resolution: 4.3.2: ovary not joined directly to the oviduct; egg crosses a short gap into its funnel (word-neutral). (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: 4.4.1 says without a condition that the chromosomes of a body cell are in homologous pairs and that each set has 'one chromosome of each kind'. 4.4.2 then teaches that Y carries no allele of an X-linked gene, so the X and Y of a male are not a matched pair. The male exception is not flagged.
issues.educational_consequence: Minor. A strong learner may be confused about why a male expresses one X-linked allele if every chromosome has a homologous partner.
issues.recommended_repair: Add a clause in 4.4.1: 'except that in males the X and Y chromosomes are different from each other'.
issues.resolution: 4.4.1 homologous chromosomes: added that in males the X and Y chromosomes differ from each other. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

affected_ids: 4.3.4 HIV and vulnerability to other illness
issues.finding: OBJ-6116-4.3.4-04 asks for the increased vulnerability of Namibians to other illness because HIV is common: a population effect. The notes explain the individual effect well, but give the population effect only as a bare statement ('TB and other infections are also more common among the population') with no reason. The reason is that more people with active TB means more TB bacteria spread, including to HIV-negative people.
issues.educational_consequence: A 'discuss' answer on this objective would stop at the individual and miss the community-level link.
issues.recommended_repair: Add one sentence: 'More people with active TB means more TB bacteria are passed on, so even people without HIV are more exposed.'
issues.resolution: 4.3.4: added population-level reason: more people with active TB pass on more TB bacteria, so people without HIV are more exposed. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: P03(g) credits 'temperatures between those tested, such as 30 °C, were not tested, so the best temperature could lie between them'. The germination notes never make this point about the gap between tested values. A learner working from the notes alone must infer it.
issues.educational_consequence: Learners who rely on the notes may miss the mark.
issues.recommended_repair: Add to 4.3.5 Investigating germination: 'The best temperature can only be placed between tested values; test more temperatures close to the highest result to find it.'
issues.resolution: 4.3.5 Investigating germination: best temperature can only be placed between values tested; test more temperatures near the highest result. (fixed in the author script and regenerated; checks re-run clean.)

issues.finding: The stem largely gives the answer away. It names the line as 'the parental genotypes' and quotes 'tall x short', so the learner only has to say that these are phenotypes. It does not make the learner tell a genotype from a phenotype without help.
issues.educational_consequence: The item checks recall of the label, not discrimination.
issues.recommended_repair: Give the learner a diagram with both lines filled in, one correct and one swapped, and ask which line is wrong and why. Or ask them to write the correct parental line for given plants.
issues.resolution: Post-review repair: exemplar generator now presents only the incomplete tall × short record and asks why it does not specify both genotypes. The answer requires identifying tall as TT or Tt and short as tt. Exemplar and topic 4 were regenerated; structural checks pass. This is an author resolution, not a second reviewer verdict.
